REST API only: AWS WAF, API keys, per-client throttling, request validation, caching, private endpoints, X-Ray tracing, response streaming
HTTP API only: JWT authorizers, automatic deployments

sources.title: Lambda quotas

Environment variables total at most 4 KB

sources.title: DynamoDB read consistency
supports: A write that returned HTTP 200 has been durably persisted
Eventually consistent reads are the default, may not reflect a recently completed write, and cost half of strongly consistent reads
ConsistentRead is available on GetItem, Query, and Scan for tables and local secondary indexes, not for global secondary indexes or streams
Global tables have two modes: multi-Region eventual consistency (default, typically replicated within a second) and multi-Region strong consistency (synchronous replication before the write returns)

sources.title: DynamoDB condition expression CLI example
supports: PutItem overwrites an item with the same primary key unless a condition prevents it
attribute_not_exists on a key attribute is true only when no item with that full key exists
A write whose condition evaluates to false is rejected with "The conditional request failed"

sources.title: Paginating table query results in DynamoDB
supports: A Query returns at most 1 MB per call
LastEvaluatedKey becomes the next ExclusiveStartKey; its absence is the only sign that the result set is finished
A non-empty LastEvaluatedKey does not guarantee that more items remain

sources.title: DynamoDB on-demand capacity mode
supports: On-demand tables are billed per read and write request, with no throughput charge at zero traffic
One read request unit is one strongly consistent read, or two eventually consistent reads, of an item up to 4 KB; one write request unit is one write of an item up to 1 KB
New on-demand tables sustain up to 4,000 writes and 12,000 reads per second and can be throttled when traffic more than doubles within 30 minutes
A maximum read or write throughput can be configured per on-demand table

sources.title: Constraints in Amazon DynamoDB
supports: Maximum item size is 400 KB
A transaction can contain at most 100 unique items and 4 MB
Sort key values are at most 1024 bytes and partition key values 2048 bytes

sources.title: Control access to HTTP APIs with JWT authorizers in API Gateway
supports: The authorizer checks signature (RSA-based algorithms only), iss, aud or client_id, exp, nbf, iat, and route scopes; a failure denies the request
client_id is evaluated only when aud is absent
Public keys are cached for up to two hours
Verified claims reach a Lambda integration at requestContext.authorizer.jwt.claims
There is no standard way to tell access tokens from ID tokens; requiring scopes on routes is recommended
For Cognito the issuer is https://cognito-idp.{region}.amazonaws.com/{userPoolId}

sources.title: Cognito: the redirect and authorization endpoint
supports: /oauth2/authorize accepts response_type, client_id, redirect_uri, state, scope, code_challenge, and code_challenge_method
Only S256 is supported for PKCE
The redirect URI must be pre-registered and HTTPS, except http://localhost
An implicit grant is described as less secure because it exposes tokens
An authorization code is valid for five minutes
An ID token is returned only when the openid scope is requested

sources.title: Cognito: understanding the access token
supports: Access tokens are signed with RS256 and carry sub, client_id, token_use = access, and scope
sub is the recommended way to identify a user
Access token validity is configurable from 5 minutes to 1 day
Managed login sets a browser cookie valid for one hour; token durations under an hour are discouraged with managed login

sources.title: Cognito: ending user sessions with token revocation
supports: Revoked tokens cannot be used with Cognito API calls, but are still valid to any JWT library that verifies only signature and expiration
Token revocation is enabled by default on new app clients

sources.title: Cognito: the managed login sign-out endpoint
supports: GET /logout with client_id and logout_uri signs the user out of managed login and redirects to an allowed sign-out URL

sources.title: What is Amazon IVS Low-Latency Streaming?
supports: IVS channels can deliver video with latency under 5 seconds; IVS stages under 300 ms
Ingest protocols are RTMP, RTMPS, and SRT
The data plane (ingest and viewing) is global; the control plane (API, channels, stream keys) is regional
Observed latency varies between users with location, network, and the components in the chain

sources.title: What is Amazon IVS Real-Time Streaming?
supports: Real-time streaming delivers latency that can be under 300 milliseconds from host to viewer
Up to 12 hosts on a stage; the resource is a stage, not a channel

sources.title: Amazon Interactive Video Service endpoints and quotas
supports: ap-northeast-1 has endpoints for IVS low-latency streaming, real-time streaming, and chat
One stream key per channel, not adjustable
Default quotas per Region: 100 concurrent streams and 15,000 concurrent views
BASIC ingest bitrate: 1.5 Mbps at 480p or less, 3.5 Mbps above 480p; STANDARD and ADVANCED: 8.5 Mbps; ingest resolution up to 1080p
PutMetadata: 1 KB payload, 5 transactions per second per channel
Real-time stages: 12 publishers and 10,000 subscribers per stage by default

sources.title: Amazon IVS Streaming Configuration
supports: Four channel types; STANDARD is the default; BASIC is transmuxed into a single rendition, STANDARD and ADVANCED are transcoded into several
Exceeding the allowed input resolution or bitrate probably disconnects the stream immediately
The RTMPS ingest URL form rtmps://<ingest endpoint>:443/app/<stream key>
Keyframe interval of 2 seconds is recommended; values above 5 seconds are to be avoided; a 2-second interval gives a stream-start latency of roughly 6 to 7 seconds
For the lowest latency the IVS player is required; H.264 video and AAC audio; CBR is recommended

sources.title: Getting started with IVS: Set Up Streaming Software
supports: OBS Studio 30.2 or later has an Amazon IVS service entry that takes the stream key
A stream lasts 48 hours at most; a reconnect starts a new stream
IVS disconnects after 30 seconds without data from the encoder
The FFmpeg example for RTMPS

sources.title: Amazon IVS Pricing
supports: All streams sent to IVS incur video input costs, even if they are not viewed; input is rounded up to the minute, output to the second
Input per hour: Basic 0.20, Standard 2.00, Advanced SD 0.50, Advanced HD 0.85 USD
Output is billed per hour delivered, by resolution (SD up to 480, HD up to 720, Full HD up to 1080) and by where viewers are served from
Japan is in the output group 'Japan, Hong Kong, and South East Asia'
Free tier for new customers, first 12 months: 5 hours of basic input and 100 hours of SD output a month
Real-time streaming is billed per participant hour
sources.note: The page describes no charge for a channel that exists but is not live.

sources.title: Amazon VPC pricing
supports: A NAT gateway is billed per NAT gateway-hour while provisioned and available, plus per GB processed regardless of source or destination; a partial hour is billed as a full hour
Standard data transfer charges apply on top of NAT gateway data processing
Every public IPv4 address is billed by the hour, in use or idle, at the same rate; Elastic IP addresses attached to NAT gateways are named as an example
A Regional NAT gateway is billed per hour for each Availability Zone it is configured in
sources.note: The page renders its regional price tables with JavaScript. The numbers in the book come from the Price List bulk API, not from this page.

sources.title: What is Amazon VPC?
supports: There is no additional charge for using a VPC; some components such as NAT gateways are charged
Private IPv4 addresses are not charged
AWS Free Tier customers get 750 hours of public IPv4 address usage with the EC2 service

sources.title: Subnets for your VPC
supports: The subnet type is determined by its routing: a public subnet has a direct route to an internet gateway, a private subnet does not and needs a NAT device for internet access, an isolated subnet has no routes to destinations outside its VPC
Network ACLs allow or deny traffic at the subnet level

sources.title: Subnet CIDR blocks
supports: A subnet's IPv4 CIDR block is between /28 and /16
The first four addresses and the last address of every subnet are reserved

sources.title: VPC CIDR blocks
supports: A VPC's IPv4 CIDR block is between /16 and /28
Some AWS services use 172.17.0.0/16, so that range is best avoided

sources.title: Route table concepts
supports: The main route table controls routing for every subnet not explicitly associated with another route table
Every route table has a local route for communication within the VPC
A route has a destination CIDR and a target such as an internet gateway

sources.title: Control traffic to your AWS resources using security groups
supports: Security groups are stateful: responses to allowed traffic are allowed regardless of the rules in the other direction

sources.title: Control subnet traffic with network access control lists
supports: Network ACLs are stateless: responses to allowed traffic are not automatically allowed
Network ACL rules are evaluated when traffic enters and leaves the subnet, not as it is routed within a subnet
The default network ACL allows all inbound and outbound traffic
sources.note: The default rules were read on the linked page https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/default-network-acl.html.

sources.title: Infrastructure security in Amazon VPC
supports: Security groups work at the instance level with allow rules only; network ACLs work at the subnet level with allow and deny rules, evaluated in ascending order
You can secure your instances using only security groups

sources.title: Enable internet access for a VPC using an internet gateway
supports: There is no charge for an internet gateway itself

sources.title: NAT gateway basics
supports: A NAT gateway is created in one Availability Zone and is redundant within that zone
If zones share one NAT gateway and its zone is down, resources in the other zones lose internet access; one NAT gateway per zone avoids this
A public NAT gateway sits in a public subnet and needs an Elastic IP address
sources.note: The Elastic IP requirement was read on https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/vpc-nat-gateway.html.

sources.title: Gateway endpoints
supports: Gateway endpoints exist for Amazon S3 and DynamoDB only, and need no internet gateway or NAT device
There is no additional charge for using gateway endpoints
Creating one adds a route to each selected route table: destination the service's prefix list, target the endpoint
Prefix lists are specific to a Region, so traffic to the service in another Region does not use the endpoint

sources.title: Access an AWS service using an interface VPC endpoint
supports: An interface endpoint creates an endpoint network interface with a private IP address in each chosen subnet, one subnet per Availability Zone
Interface endpoints are billed for hourly usage and for data processing
Private DNS needs DNS hostnames and DNS resolution enabled on the VPC
The endpoint's security group must allow inbound HTTPS from the resources that call it

sources.title: AWS PrivateLink pricing
supports: An interface endpoint is billed for each hour it stays provisioned in each Availability Zone; a partial hour is billed as a full hour
Data processing is billed per GB regardless of the traffic's source or destination, in tiers over the Region's monthly total

sources.title: Giving Lambda functions access to resources in an Amazon VPC
supports: By default a Lambda function can reach the public internet; attached to a VPC it can reach only what the VPC can
Connecting a function to a public subnet gives it neither internet access nor a public IP address

The execution role needs ec2:CreateNetworkInterface, DescribeNetworkInterfaces, DescribeSubnets, DeleteNetworkInterface, AssignPrivateIpAddresses, and UnassignPrivateIpAddresses on all resources, and the function's code is implicitly granted them too
A new function stays Pending while Lambda creates the Hyperplane ENI, which can take several minutes; functions with the same subnets and security groups share one
After 14 idle days Lambda reclaims unused Hyperplane ENIs and the function becomes Inactive

sources.title: Amazon ECR interface VPC endpoints (AWS PrivateLink)
supports: Fargate tasks on platform version 1.4.0 or later need both ECR endpoints (ecr.api, ecr.dkr) and the S3 gateway endpoint to pull images privately
Fargate tasks that use the awslogs driver in a VPC without an internet gateway need the com.amazonaws.region.logs interface endpoint

sources.title: Fargate task networking
supports: A Fargate task pulls its image over a public IP address in a public subnet, a NAT gateway from a private subnet, or ECR interface endpoints

sources.title: Improve the security of EC2 instances by using VPC endpoints for Systems Manager

ssmmessages is required for Session Manager

sources.title: AWS Availability Zones
supports: Each Region has at least three Availability Zones
An AZ ID such as apne1-az1 is the same physical location in every account; ap-northeast-1 has apne1-az1 to apne1-az4
AWS may restrict new resources in a constrained Availability Zone

sources.title: AZ IDs for your AWS resources

`aws ec2 describe-availability-zones` lists the zone names and IDs of an account

sources.title: AWS Fault Isolation Boundaries: Availability Zones
supports: An Availability Zone is one or more discrete data centers with separate power, networking, and connectivity inside one Region
Zones in a Region are up to about 100 km apart and designed not to fail together

sources.title: AWS Fault Isolation Boundaries: Regions
supports: Regions are isolated from each other, which limits a service failure to one Region
Resources and data in one Region do not exist in another unless you replicate them

supports: Export names must be unique within a Region for each AWS account

CloudFormation documents Fn::GetStackOutput for references across accounts or Regions

sources.title: Amazon VPCs and ElastiCache security
supports: All node-based ElastiCache clusters are launched in a VPC; ElastiCache Serverless caches can also be configured with a public endpoint that needs no VPC configuration

sources.title: Inference using Converse API
supports: Converse needs bedrock:InvokeModel; ConverseStream needs bedrock:InvokeModelWithResponseStream
Order of ConverseStream events: messageStart, content block events, messageStop (with stopReason), metadata (usage and metrics)
contentBlockStart is sent for tool use only; a text delta is {contentBlockDelta: {delta: {text}, contentBlockIndex}}
Shape of a Converse response: output.message.content[].text, stopReason, usage, metrics

sources.title: Creating and verifying identities in Amazon SES
supports: An identity is a domain or an email address, verified separately in each Region
Verifying a domain covers its addresses and subdomains

Email address identities are case-sensitive; the verification mail comes from no-reply-aws@amazon.com and its link expires after 24 hours
A domain identity is verified by publishing three Easy DKIM CNAME records, which can take up to 72 hours to be detected
The CNAME value is the token followed by the SigningHostedZone returned by CreateEmailIdentity and GetEmailIdentity

sources.title: Using a custom MAIL FROM domain

It needs exactly one MX record `10 feedback-smtp.<region>.amazonses.com` and a TXT record "v=spf1 include:amazonses.com ~all"
Behavior on MX failure is either falling back to the default MAIL FROM domain or rejecting the message
SES looks for the MX record for up to 72 hours

sources.title: Complying with DMARC authentication protocol in Amazon SES
supports: SPF checks the MAIL FROM domain, DKIM checks the signing domain, and DMARC requires one of them to align with the From domain
A message passes DMARC if either the SPF or the DKIM alignment check passes
The DMARC policy is a TXT record at _dmarc.<domain>; p=none, quarantine, and reject, rolled out in that order
SPF alignment through SES needs a custom MAIL FROM domain; DKIM alignment needs Easy DKIM on the From domain
`dig TXT _dmarc.<domain>` shows the published policy

sources.title: What is Amazon Aurora DSQL?
supports: Aurora DSQL is available in Asia Pacific (Tokyo), ap-northeast-1
Serverless, with no instances to provision; data is replicated synchronously across three Availability Zones
Currently compatible with PostgreSQL version 16
ACID transactions with strong consistency and snapshot isolation
Multi-Region clusters must stay inside one Region set; Tokyo, Osaka, and Seoul are in the Asia Pacific set

sources.title: Migrating from PostgreSQL to Aurora DSQL
supports: The isolation level is fixed at PostgreSQL Repeatable Read
DDL and DML need separate transactions; a transaction holds one DDL statement; a transaction modifies at most 3,000 rows
Connections time out after 1 hour
One built-in database named postgres per cluster; UTF-8, C collation only, UTC
No temporary tables, no triggers, no PL/pgSQL (SQL functions only); DELETE FROM or DROP/CREATE instead of TRUNCATE; CREATE INDEX ASYNC instead of CREATE INDEX
Foreign keys are supported
Conflicts return a serialization error instead of waiting for a lock; AWS recommends idempotent transactions with retry, and random primary keys
Permissions are schema-level grants: admin manages objects in public, non-admin roles use user-created schemas

sources.title: Supported SQL for Aurora DSQL
supports: BEGIN accepts ISOLATION LEVEL REPEATABLE READ and READ WRITE | READ ONLY
INSERT supports ON CONFLICT; SELECT supports FOR UPDATE and FOR KEY SHARE, joins, CTEs, and window functions
CREATE SCHEMA, CREATE VIEW, CREATE SEQUENCE, CREATE FUNCTION ... LANGUAGE SQL, and CREATE [UNIQUE] INDEX ASYNC are supported
The page says the list is not exhaustive

sources.title: DDL and distributed transactions in Aurora DSQL
supports: A transaction can contain only one DDL statement and cannot mix DDL and DML
A schema change updates the catalog version; a session holding an older cached catalog can receive SQLSTATE 40001 with OCC code OC001, and a retry typically succeeds

sources.title: Concurrency control in Aurora DSQL
supports: Optimistic concurrency control: conflicts are evaluated at commit time, without locks
A conflict is returned as SQLSTATE 40001; OC000 is a data conflict, OC001 a schema conflict
Of two transactions that modified the same row, the one that commits first succeeds
SELECT ... FOR UPDATE is adjudicated at commit as if the transaction wrote the rows
AWS recommends retrying, with idempotent transactions, and random primary keys to avoid contention on a few keys

sources.title: Cluster quotas and database limits in Amazon Aurora DSQL
supports: 3,000 rows mutated per transaction, 10 MiB of data modified per write transaction, 5 minutes maximum transaction time, 60 minutes maximum connection duration
10,000 connections per cluster by default, 100 new connections per second with a burst of 1,000
1 database per cluster, 10 schemas per database, 1,000 tables per database, 24 indexes per table, 2 MiB per row
20 single-Region clusters per account per Region by default

sources.title: Aurora DSQL: CREATE TABLE
supports: CREATE TABLE supports IF NOT EXISTS, CHECK, DEFAULT, UNIQUE, PRIMARY KEY, REFERENCES / FOREIGN KEY with referential actions, and identity columns
CASCADE, SET NULL, and SET DEFAULT actions count toward the per-transaction row limit

sources.title: Aurora DSQL: ALTER TABLE
supports: ADD COLUMN takes a column name and a data type; the supported syntax lists no constraint or default on that form
CHECK and FOREIGN KEY constraints added to an existing table must be NOT VALID and are validated with ALTER TABLE ASYNC ... VALIDATE CONSTRAINT
The listed actions include DROP NOT NULL but no SET NOT NULL and no change of a column's type

sources.title: Aurora DSQL: CREATE INDEX
supports: Index creation is always asynchronous, so the ASYNC keyword must be specified
CREATE [UNIQUE] INDEX ASYNC supports IF NOT EXISTS, INCLUDE, and a WHERE predicate

sources.title: Asynchronous indexes in Aurora DSQL
supports: CREATE INDEX ASYNC returns a job_id immediately
sys.jobs has job_id, status (submitted, processing, failed, completed), and details
A failed build leaves the index INVALID until it is dropped; completed and failed jobs are removed from sys.jobs after 30 minutes
sources.note: The page names sys.wait_for_job but shows no complete call, so the sample polls sys.jobs instead.

sources.title: Working with foreign key constraints in Aurora DSQL
supports: Foreign keys are checked against the transaction snapshot and again at commit; a violation by a concurrent transaction surfaces as a serialization error
Updating a non-key column of the referenced row does not conflict with an insert that references it
DML on referenced or referencing tables incurs extra reads

sources.title: Aurora DSQL: Working with sequences and identity columns
supports: UUIDs are the recommended default identifier type; sequences and identity columns exist for when integers are needed
CREATE SEQUENCE requires an explicit CACHE of 1 or at least 65536 (stated on the CREATE SEQUENCE page, which was read too)

sources.title: Primary keys in Aurora DSQL
supports: A primary key cannot be changed or added after the table is created
For tables with many writes, AWS advises against monotonically increasing integer keys and for randomly distributed ones

sources.title: Authentication and authorization for Aurora DSQL
supports: dsql:DbConnectAdmin connects as the admin role; dsql:DbConnect connects as a custom database role
AWS IAM GRANT associates a database role with an IAM identity
After revoking the IAM permission, existing connections can stay authorized until they end

sources.title: Generating an authentication token in Amazon Aurora DSQL
supports: The token is the password, used only when a connection is established; an open connection stays valid after the token expires
Tokens expire after 15 minutes by default, one week at most
Generating a token is a local signing operation that does not contact AWS
The cluster endpoint has the form <cluster id>.dsql.<region>.on.aws
The JavaScript signer is DsqlSigner in @aws-sdk/dsql-signer, with getDbConnectAuthToken and getDbConnectAdminAuthToken

sources.title: Aurora DSQL: Using database roles and IAM authentication
supports: CREATE ROLE ... WITH LOGIN, then AWS IAM GRANT <role> TO '<IAM role ARN>', then GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA and GRANT ... ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA
sys.iam_pg_role_mappings lists the mappings, with arn and pg_role_name columns

supports: AWS publishes authentication plugins for node-postgres and for Postgres.js

A user named admin gets an admin token, any other user a regular one
sources.note: The sample does not use the connector; it passes the same signer to node-postgres directly, as the AWS Lambda sample does.

supports: AWS lists driver samples for node-postgres, node-postgres on AWS Lambda, and Postgres.js
AWS lists an adapter for Drizzle ORM and samples for Prisma, Sequelize, and TypeORM

sources.title: aws-samples/aurora-dsql-samples: Using AWS Lambda with Amazon Aurora DSQL
supports: A Lambda function defined without a VPC connects with node-postgres, passing a function that calls DsqlSigner as the pool's password
The pool is kept in a module-level variable and shared between invocations
The sample builds the endpoint as <identifier>.dsql.<region>.on.aws and says an admin database role is not good practice for production

sources.title: Aurora DSQL cluster lifecycle
supports: A cluster without connection activity becomes Idle and then Inactive, where running resources are scaled to zero and data is kept
Connecting wakes it; the first connection to an Idle or Inactive cluster is slower
A backup needs an Active cluster

sources.title: Backup and restore for Amazon Aurora DSQL
supports: Backups go through AWS Backup: full cluster backups, on demand or on a schedule with retention
A restore always creates a new cluster
sources.note: The page does not describe point-in-time recovery for Aurora DSQL.

sources.title: How billing works in Aurora DSQL
supports: Activity is metered in DPUs (compute, read, and write components) and storage in GB-month
Worked examples: a point lookup of 0.00675 DPU and a single-row insert of 0.06175 DPU
sources.note: The examples' DPU figures are used as stand-ins in the chapter's cost scenario. Nothing was measured.

sources.title: Amazon Aurora DSQL pricing
supports: Billed for DPUs and for storage in GB-month; an idle cluster incurs no DPU charges
Each month the first 100,000 DPUs and 1 GB of storage are free
Backups are billed through AWS Backup
sources.note: The page shows prices through a script; the numbers in the book come from the Price List. The page does not say whether the free tier ends.

sources.title: Managing and connecting to Amazon Aurora DSQL clusters using AWS PrivateLink
supports: The default cluster host name is a public DNS name; interface VPC endpoints are an option for private connectivity
Connecting through an endpoint's own DNS name or IP address does not support verify-full

sources.title: Troubleshooting issues in Aurora DSQL
supports: After an error during COMMIT the transaction might have committed; AWS says to design transactions to be idempotent
'Wrong user to action mapping' means the token type does not match the database role
A connection is rejected when the assumed role's credentials have expired, even if the token has not

sources.title: Considerations for working with Amazon Aurora DSQL
supports: GRANT and REVOKE changes reach existing connections within the connection lifetime; a new connection sees them at once
A connection should be refreshed to see schemas and tables created in another connection

sources.title: Release notes for Aurora DSQL

Identity columns and sequences were added on February 13, 2026; partial indexes on September 15, 2026

sources.title: Configuring SSL/TLS certificates for Aurora DSQL connections
supports: The server certificate chains to Amazon Root CA 1; AWS recommends verify-full for production

sources.title: Scaling to Zero ACUs with automatic pause and resume for Aurora serverless
supports: Auto-pause is a minimum capacity of 0 ACUs; before it existed the lowest minimum was 0.5 ACUs
An instance pauses after 300 to 86,400 seconds without user connections (default 300)
A paused instance has no instance charge; storage is still charged
Resuming takes about 15 seconds, and 30 seconds or longer after more than 24 hours paused
An open user connection, an associated RDS Proxy, logical replication, or a zero-ETL integration keeps instances from pausing
Aurora PostgreSQL needs 16.3, 15.7, 14.12, 13.15 or higher

sources.title: Download and upload objects with presigned URLs
supports: A presigned URL uses the credentials of the principal who generated it, and its capabilities are limited by that principal's permissions
Presigned URLs are bearer tokens that grant access to those who possess them, and can be used multiple times until they expire
A presigned URL made with temporary credentials expires when those credentials expire, even if a later expiration was requested
With the AWS CLI or SDKs the expiration can be set as high as 7 days
S3 checks the expiration at the time of the HTTP request
A bucket policy can deny presigned requests by signature age with the s3:signatureAge condition key
sources.note: The page gives typical credential lifetimes for EC2 instance profiles, ECS tasks, and STS AssumeRole. It gives none for a Lambda execution role.

sources.title: Uploading objects with presigned URLs
supports: An upload to a key that already exists replaces the existing object
The content type in the upload request must match the one given when the presigned PUT URL was generated

sources.title: POST Policy
supports: A POST policy holds an expiration and a list of conditions the request must meet
content-length-range sets the minimum and maximum allowable size of the uploaded content
Conditions support exact matching and starts-with matching on fields such as key and Content-Type
Each form field except x-amz-signature, file, policy, and x-ignore- fields must appear in the list of conditions
sources.note: On 2026-10-11 the older path /AmazonS3/latest/API/sigv4-HTTPPOSTConstructPolicy.html redirected to the API reference index; the page was read at the /developerguide/ path. Its conditions table does not list the tagging field by name.

sources.title: POST Object
supports: The file must be the last field in the form
POST Object has a tagging form field that takes an XML tag set
success_action_status defaults to 204
A request without a policy is anonymous and works only on publicly writable buckets
sources.note: Read at the /developerguide/ path, as the /API/ path redirected to the index on 2026-10-11.

sources.title: Authenticating Requests: Using Query Parameters (AWS Signature Version 4)
supports: X-Amz-Expires is between 1 and 604800 seconds
The host header and any x-amz-* headers must be signed, and signing every header you plan to send is recommended
A presigned URL made with STS credentials carries X-Amz-Security-Token
sources.note: The page does not state a rule for content-length specifically. That a signed Content-Length pins the size of a presigned PUT was not confirmed.

sources.title: How to prevent object overwrites with conditional writes
supports: If-None-Match prevents overwriting an existing key
If-None-Match can be used with PutObject, CompleteMultipartUpload, and CopyObject; POST Object is not in the list

sources.title: HeadObject
supports: For a key that does not exist, S3 returns 404 if the caller has s3:ListBucket on the bucket and 403 if it does not

sources.title: Expiring objects
supports: In a nonversioned bucket, S3 queues an expired object for removal and removes it asynchronously
Tag-based filters are evaluated daily, and the object's current tags are re-evaluated when the action executes; if the tag is gone, the expiration does not proceed
There may be a delay between the expiration date and the removal, and expired objects are not charged for storage
A bucket policy cannot prevent deletions by a lifecycle rule

sources.title: Configuring a bucket lifecycle configuration to delete incomplete multipart uploads
supports: AWS recommends a lifecycle rule with AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload to minimize storage costs
The rule aborts multipart uploads not completed within the given number of days and deletes their parts; it deletes no objects

sources.title: Tagging your objects
supports: Tags can be set in a POST Object request
Lifecycle rules can filter on object tags
DELETE Object tagging removes the tag set without a request charge, where PUT Object tagging is billed as a Tier 1 request

sources.title: Using cross-origin resource sharing (CORS)
supports: S3 uses the first CORS rule whose origin, method, and requested headers match the request
ACLs and policies continue to apply when CORS is enabled

sources.title: Elements of a CORS configuration
supports: AllowedMethods accepts GET, PUT, POST, DELETE, and HEAD
AllowedOrigins lists the origins allowed to make cross-origin requests

sources.title: Blocking public access to your Amazon S3 storage
supports: The four settings BlockPublicAcls, IgnorePublicAcls, BlockPublicPolicy, and RestrictPublicBuckets

sources.title: What is Amazon S3? (Strong consistency)
supports: S3 provides strong read-after-write consistency for PUT and DELETE of objects, and reads of object tags and metadata such as HEAD are strongly consistent
sources.note: The sentence names PUT and DELETE. It does not name POST Object.

sources.title: nitropack 2.13.4 (npm tarball: dist/presets/aws-lambda)
supports: The preset is named `aws-lambda`; its only option is `awsLambda.streaming` (boolean, default false)

With streaming true the entry is `awslambda.streamifyResponse(...)`, writes metadata through `awslambda.HttpResponseStream.from`, and adds `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`
Both entries rebuild the Cookie header from the event's `cookies` array and decode a base64 request body as UTF-8 text
.output/nitro.json records the preset and `config.awsLambda.streaming`

sources.title: Restrict access to an AWS Lambda function URL origin
supports: To use OAC the function URL's AuthType must be AWS_IAM
CloudFront needs lambda:InvokeFunctionUrl and lambda:InvokeFunction, granted to cloudfront.amazonaws.com with the distribution as source ARN
For PUT or POST, the viewer must send the SHA256 of the body in x-amz-content-sha256; Lambda does not support unsigned payloads
With signing behavior `always`, CloudFront signs every origin request; `no-override` passes a viewer Authorization header through instead

sources.title: Control access to Lambda function URLs
supports: AuthType AWS_IAM authenticates and authorizes requests with IAM; NONE performs no authentication
Starting in October 2025, new function URLs require both lambda:InvokeFunctionUrl and lambda:InvokeFunction
Without those permissions in the resource-based policy, callers get 403 Forbidden

sources.title: Invoking Lambda function URLs
supports: Function URL events and responses follow API Gateway payload format version 2.0
Request cookies arrive in a `cookies` array; response cookies are returned in a `cookies` array

sources.title: Invoking a response streaming enabled function using Lambda function URLs
supports: InvokeMode BUFFERED is the default, uses the Invoke API, and has a 6 MB maximum payload
InvokeMode RESPONSE_STREAM uses InvokeWithResponseStream and has a 200 MB maximum response payload
sources.note: The page does not describe what a client receives when the invoke mode and the handler type disagree.

sources.title: Select a method to invoke your Lambda function using an HTTP request
supports: Function URLs have no charge beyond Lambda's own; authentication is IAM or none
API Gateway adds authorizers, throttling, request validation, custom domain names, and WAF integration
A function URL answers HTTP 429 once the function's concurrency limit is reached

sources.title: Response streaming for Lambda functions
supports: Streaming is available through function URLs, InvokeWithResponseStream, and the API Gateway proxy integration
Streamed responses can be up to 200 MB; buffered ones up to 6 MB
The first 6 MB is uncapped; the rest is limited to 2 MBps
Managed Node.js runtimes support streaming
A streamed response is not stopped when the client disconnects; the full duration is billed
Function URLs do not support response streaming inside a VPC

sources.title: Manage how long content stays in the cache (expiration)
supports: With minimum TTL 0, CloudFront respects Cache-Control: no-cache, no-store, and private from the origin
With minimum TTL above 0, CloudFront caches for the minimum TTL even when those directives are present
With both max-age and s-maxage, CloudFront uses the lesser of s-maxage and the maximum TTL; browsers use max-age
Without Cache-Control, CloudFront caches for the default TTL
CloudFront supports stale-while-revalidate and stale-if-error, bounded by the maximum TTL

sources.title: Understand cache policies
supports: Values in the cache key are automatically included in origin requests
Cookies set to None are not in the cache key and not automatically sent to the origin
Minimum, maximum, and default TTL all 0 disables caching

sources.title: Cache content based on cookies
supports: By default CloudFront ignores cookies and removes them before forwarding a request to the origin
When cookies are forwarded, CloudFront caches Set-Cookie with the object and sends it on every cache hit
With cookies not forwarded, CloudFront removes Set-Cookie from responses before returning them
sources.note: The page is written in terms of the legacy forwarding settings. Whether Set-Cookie is removed under a cache policy with cookies set to None was not confirmed, which is why the stack also removes it with a response headers policy.

sources.title: Understand response headers policies
supports: Removed headers are removed from every response sent to viewers, whether served from the cache or from the origin
Set-Cookie is not in the list of headers that cannot be removed

sources.title: Serve compressed files
supports: CloudFront compresses only when the origin response has a Content-Length header, between 1,000 and 10,000,000 bytes
A response with Content-Encoding is passed through uncompressed-by-CloudFront
Compression needs Gzip or Brotli enabled in the cache policy

sources.title: How CloudFront processes HTTP 4xx and 5xx status codes from your origin
supports: CloudFront caches 404, 414, and 5xx responses for the error caching minimum TTL, 10 seconds by default
With the CachingDisabled managed policy, those status codes are not cached
CloudFront caches responses to GET and HEAD, optionally OPTIONS, and no other method
sources.note: How a `no-store` on a 404 interacts with the 10-second error caching minimum TTL is not stated plainly on the page.

sources.title: Origin settings
supports: The default origin response timeout is 30 seconds

sources.title: Working with Lambda environment variables

sources.title: MDN: Set-Cookie header

SameSite=Lax sends the cookie on same-site requests and on a limited set of cross-site navigations
A __Host- cookie must be Secure, set from HTTPS, have no Domain, and have Path=/

sources.title: X-Ray SDK and Daemon Support timeline
supports: The X-Ray SDKs and daemon entered maintenance mode on February 25th, 2026: releases are limited to security issues, with no new features
The page lists no end date for maintenance mode
AWS recommends migrating to OpenTelemetry for instrumenting applications and sending traces to AWS X-Ray
sources.note: The page is about the SDKs and the daemon. It says nothing about the X-Ray service ending; traces are still sent to X-Ray.

sources.title: Migrating from X-Ray instrumentation to OpenTelemetry instrumentation
supports: For Lambda, the options are an auto-instrumentation layer (recommended: AWS Lambda Layer for OpenTelemetry; also the AWS managed Lambda layer for ADOT) or a manual setup with a simple span processor, an X-Ray UDP span exporter and an X-Ray Lambda propagator
To use only tracing with the AWS Lambda Layer for OpenTelemetry, set OTEL_AWS_APPLICATION_SIGNALS_ENABLED=false
When sent to X-Ray, server spans become segments, other spans become subsegments, and attributes become metadata by default

sources.title: Migrate to OpenTelemetry Node.js
supports: Manual spans in a Lambda function that has the layer are created with @opentelemetry/api, whose version is recommended to match the one the ADOT JavaScript SDK uses

sources.title: AWS Distro for OpenTelemetry: Lambda
supports: The layer is enabled with AWS_LAMBDA_EXEC_WRAPPER=/opt/otel-instrument, and its ARN is listed per Region and language
On 2026-10-12 the Node.js ARN for ap-northeast-1 was arn:aws:lambda:ap-northeast-1:615299751070:layer:AWSOpenTelemetryDistroJs:16
Supported Node.js runtimes listed: 18.x, 20.x, 22.x. Node.js 24.x is not in the list
By default only the AWS SDK and HTTP instrumentations are enabled; sampling is parent-based and adjustable with OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER

supports: The AWS Lambda Layer for OpenTelemetry is also a component of Lambda OpenTelemetry support and provides tracing

sources.title: Visualize Lambda function invocations using AWS X-Ray
supports: With Active tracing Lambda records two segments per trace for sampled requests; PassThrough only forwards the tracing header
The sampling rate is 1 request per second and 5 percent of additional requests, and it cannot be configured for functions
The execution role needs xray:PutTraceSegments and xray:PutTelemetryRecords
An upstream service's tracing header decides whether Lambda sends a trace

sources.title: Instrumenting Node.js code in AWS Lambda
supports: Lambda's Node.js guide offers ADOT layers or the X-Ray SDK for Node.js to send trace data to X-Ray

sources.title: Log and monitor Node.js Lambda functions
supports: In the text format the Node.js runtime adds a timestamp, the request ID and a log level in front of each line the function logs
With the JSON log format Lambda doesn't double-encode logs that are already JSON encoded
Code that emits embedded metric format with console.log should write to process.stdout instead when the log format is JSON
Log-level filtering needs a level and an RFC 3339 timestamp in the JSON; without a valid timestamp Lambda assigns INFO

sources.title: Configuring JSON and plain text log formats
supports: The default log format for all Lambda runtimes is plain text
The log format applies to both system logs and application logs, and JSON formatting can increase the size of log messages

sources.title: Types of metrics for Lambda functions
supports: Errors counts invocations that end in a function error: exceptions the code throws and those the runtime throws, such as timeouts
Throttled requests count as neither Invocations nor Errors
Duration supports percentile statistics and does not include cold start time
ConcurrentExecutions is read with the Max statistic

sources.title: Monitor CloudWatch metrics for HTTP APIs in API Gateway
supports: HTTP API metrics: 4xx, 5xx, Count, IntegrationLatency, Latency, DataProcessed, sent in one-minute periods
Latency runs from receiving the request to returning the response; IntegrationLatency is the backend part
Route-level metrics need detailed metrics to be enabled

sources.title: Configure logging for HTTP APIs in API Gateway
supports: An HTTP API stage can write access logs to a CloudWatch Logs group in a format built from $context variables

sources.title: DynamoDB metrics and dimensions
supports: ThrottledRequests, SystemErrors, SuccessfulRequestLatency and ConditionalCheckFailedRequests exist as table metrics
SystemErrors counts requests that generate an HTTP 500

sources.title: Configuring how CloudWatch alarms treat missing data
supports: Missing data points can be treated as notBreaching, breaching, ignore or missing; the default is missing
For a metric that reports only when an error occurs, notBreaching is the suggested treatment
When points are missing, CloudWatch evaluates over a wider evaluation range than the evaluation periods

sources.title: Alarm evaluation
supports: Datapoints to Alarm (M) out of Evaluation Periods (N): the breaching points need not be consecutive

sources.title: Using math expressions with CloudWatch metrics
supports: IF(condition, trueValue, falseValue) with a time series compared to a scalar; the result is 0 when the chosen metric has no data point at that time
FILL in an alarm can leave the alarm stuck when the latest minute never has data; an M out of N alarm is the suggested workaround

sources.title: Notifying users on alarm changes
supports: An email subscription to the SNS topic stays pending until the recipient confirms it

sources.title: CloudWatch Logs Insights language query syntax
supports: Commands are separated by the pipe character; fields, filter, stats, sort and limit are commands
Queries are charged by data scanned: select only the needed log groups and the narrowest time range

sources.title: Logs Insights: filter
supports: Conditions are combined with and / or; string values are written in double quotes, as in filter requestId = "1234656"
Field indexes speed up equality filters; filters with like do not use them

sources.title: Logs Insights: stats
supports: stats count(*) by field groups and counts, and an alias is given with as

sources.title: Supported logs and discovered fields
supports: For Lambda logs, fields are discovered automatically only for the first embedded JSON fragment in each log event
Lambda logs get @requestId, @duration, @billedDuration, @maxMemoryUsed, and @xrayTraceId when the line has a trace ID
Field discovery is supported only in the Standard log class

sources.title: Creating metrics from log events using filters
supports: Metric filters are not retroactive: they publish data points only for events after the filter was created
The default value is reported for periods in which logs are ingested and nothing matches; with no logs at all, nothing is reported
A filter with dimensions cannot have a default value, and each distinct dimension value creates another metric
Delivery to the metric is at least once; duplicates may occasionally occur

sources.title: Filter pattern syntax for metric filters
supports: JSON patterns are written in braces with $. property selectors, and combined with && and ||, as in { ($.user.id = 1) && ($.users[0].email = "John.Doe@example.com") }

sources.title: Embedding metrics within logs
supports: Embedded metric format needs logs:PutLogEvents and not cloudwatch:PutMetricData; charges are log ingestion and storage plus the custom metrics generated
A high-cardinality dimension such as requestId creates one custom metric per distinct value
Delivery is at least once; duplicate metric values may occasionally occur

sources.title: Embedded metric format specification
supports: The log event must be a valid JSON object with no additional data at the beginning or end
At most 100 metric definitions per event and 30 dimension keys per dimension set

sources.title: Working with log groups and log streams
supports: By default log data is stored indefinitely; retention is set per log group
Expired log events are not deleted immediately; it can take up to 72 hours

sources.title: AWS X-Ray concepts
supports: Trace data is retained for 30 days
The tracing header is X-Amzn-Trace-Id, with Root, Parent and Sampled fields
By default the first request each second and five percent of additional requests are recorded

sources.title: Sending trace data to AWS X-Ray
supports: X-Ray accepts trace IDs that follow the W3C Trace Context specification, written in X-Ray's format: 4efaaf4d1e8720b39541901950019ee5 becomes 1-4efaaf4d-1e8720b39541901950019ee5

sources.title: Configuring sampling rules
supports: X-Ray sampling is parent-based: the decision is made once by the first service, and downstream services honor it regardless of their own rules
The default is a reservoir of one request per second plus five percent of the rest

sources.title: Amazon SQS and AWS X-Ray
supports: SQS carries the trace header in the AWSTraceHeader message system attribute, which does not count against message size or attribute quotas
With a Lambda consumer, trace context propagation is automatic

sources.title: OTLP Endpoints
supports: Traces can be sent over OTLP/HTTP to https://xray.<region>.amazonaws.com/v1/traces with Signature Version 4

sources.title: Transaction Search
supports: With Transaction Search enabled, spans sent to X-Ray are ingested as logs in the aws/spans log group

sources.title: W3C Trace Context
supports: traceparent is version-traceid-parentid-flags: 2, 32, 16 and 2 lowercase hex characters
Version ff is invalid, and an all-zero trace-id or parent-id is forbidden
The lowest bit of trace-flags is the sampled flag

sources.title: CloudWatch RUM
supports: RUM collects client-side data from real user sessions: page load times, client-side errors and user behavior for web applications
An app monitor generates a snippet for the page, and collects from a chosen percentage of sessions
Data is retained for 30 days; copies can be sent to CloudWatch Logs to keep them longer
With X-Ray active tracing on the app monitor, client page requests appear connected to the services they call

sources.title: Synthetic monitoring (canaries)
supports: Canaries are scripts that run on a schedule, as often as once per minute, and check endpoints even when there is no customer traffic
Canaries create Lambda functions in the account and publish metrics in the CloudWatchSynthetics namespace

supports: Expired items that are not filtered keep showing in read and write operations until the background process deletes them

sources.title: Working with items and attributes in DynamoDB
supports: UpdateItem can implement an atomic counter: a numeric attribute incremented without interfering with other write requests; all write requests are applied in the order received
Atomic counter updates are not idempotent, so a retried UpdateItem can overcount; the page recommends a conditional update where miscounting cannot be tolerated
A conditional write whose condition evaluates to false still consumes write capacity (a minimum of 1 unit)

ADD supports only number and set data types
An update expression can combine SET and ADD clauses

sources.title: What is Amazon ElastiCache?
supports: ElastiCache runs in two formats: serverless caches and node-based clusters, with the Valkey, Memcached, and Redis OSS engines
ElastiCache Serverless supports two connection types, VPC and Public; a public endpoint is reached over the internet without a VPC and requires IAM authentication and TLS 1.3 for every connection
The connection type is chosen when the cache is created
ElastiCache Serverless is compatible with Valkey 7.2 and later, Memcached 1.6.22 and later, and Redis OSS 7.1; public endpoints need Valkey 9.0 or later

sources.title: Choosing between deployment options
supports: Serverless operates engines in cluster mode enabled only; clients must support cluster mode
Serverless: clients connect to a single endpoint; encryption in transit and at rest are always enabled
Serverless: data is replicated asynchronously across multiple Availability Zones; durability (the Multi-AZ transactional log) is not supported
Node-based clusters: public endpoints are not supported; pricing is per node-hour, while serverless is billed for data stored in GB-hours and requests in ECPUs
Serverless configuration is limited to basic settings such as subnets, backups, and maximum cache usage limits

sources.title: Create a Valkey serverless cache with a public endpoint
supports: Public endpoints are available on ElastiCache Serverless for Valkey 9.0 or later
ElastiCache provides a system-managed IAM user (default.iam-user) and user group (default.iam-user-group); a custom group must contain only users that authenticate with IAM
The CLI example creates the cache with --engine valkey --major-engine-version 9 --connection-type public --user-group-id default.iam-user-group
The ability to create public caches can be restricted with the elasticache:ConnectionType condition key

sources.title: Connect to a cache with a public endpoint
supports: All public endpoint connections require IAM authentication and TLS 1.3
The caller needs elasticache:Connect on both the serverless cache ARN and the ElastiCache user ARN
Three ways to produce the token: the GLIDE client, the Developer Toolkit for ElastiCache (Python), or manual SigV4 signing

Tokens are valid for 15 minutes; with the toolkit or manual signing a new token is generated for each new connection; expiry does not affect established connections; a token signed with temporary credentials expires with them if sooner
Connections expire after 12 hours; revoking elasticache:Connect does not disconnect active sessions
Troubleshooting: WRONGPASS (expired token, wrong user, missing permission, cache name not lowercase), NOAUTH when a client sends a command before authenticating, TLS handshake failure without TLS 1.3

sources.title: Authenticating with IAM
supports: IAM authentication passes a short-lived token instead of a password in AUTH or HELLO; it needs Valkey 7.2 or above (or Redis OSS 7.0 or above) and in-transit encryption

The token is a SigV4 pre-signed GET request to http://<cache name>/ with query parameters Action=connect, User=<user id>, and ResourceType=ServerlessCache for serverless caches, signed for service elasticache with a 900-second expiry, with the http:// prefix removed
For IAM-enabled users the user name and user ID must be identical
Cache names are lowercased at creation, and the signing code must use the lowercase name
An IAM-authenticated connection is disconnected after 12 hours unless re-authenticated
GLIDE 2.2 and later generate, cache, and refresh the token themselves
sources.note: The reference implementation on the page is Java. The sample's TypeScript signer follows it and was never presented to ElastiCache.

sources.title: Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)
supports: ElastiCache users carry an access string and belong to user groups, which are attached to caches
ElastiCache configures a default user with full access; the page tells you to replace it with one that is disabled or has a strong password
The nopass option is not recommended

sources.title: ElastiCache in-transit encryption (TLS)
supports: All serverless caches have in-transit encryption enabled; node-based clusters can turn it on or off
Caches with a public endpoint require TLS 1.3

sources.title: Supported and restricted Valkey, Memcached, and Redis OSS commands
supports: EVAL and EVALSHA are listed among the commands supported by serverless caches

sources.title: Scaling ElastiCache Serverless clusters
supports: A maximum can be set on cache data storage and on ECPUs per second to control cost
At the storage maximum ElastiCache evicts keys that have a TTL, and writes fail with an out-of-memory error when nothing can be evicted; above the ECPU maximum requests are throttled
A minimum usage limit is billed even when actual usage is lower
sources.note: Neither this page nor the API reference pages for DataStorage and ECPUPerSecond state the smallest accepted maximum. The stack's ECPU maximum of 1,000 is the value the page uses in its CLI example for a minimum.

sources.title: Engine versions and upgrading in ElastiCache
supports: All features available with Redis OSS 7.2 are available in Valkey 7.2 and above
Some existing ElastiCache for Redis OSS engines can be upgraded to a Valkey engine
ElastiCache versions 9.0 and 9.1 for Valkey exist

sources.title: Amazon ElastiCache pricing
supports: Serverless is billed for data stored (GB-hours, from an hourly average) and for ECPUs; a read or write uses 1 ECPU per KB transferred, and commands needing more vCPU time use proportionally more
Minimum metered data storage is 100 MB per cache for ElastiCache Serverless for Valkey and 1 GB for Memcached and Redis OSS
Billing starts when a serverless cache becomes available and continues until it is deleted
Accounts created before 2025-07-15 get 750 hours of cache.t3.micro for 12 months, which excludes ElastiCache Serverless; newer accounts get credits instead
Serverless with a public endpoint: no data transfer charge on the cache side, and USD 0.01 per GB in or out of the application within the same Region
Valkey is priced 33% lower than the other engines on Serverless and 20% lower on nodes

Every key a script accesses must be passed explicitly as a key argument, in standalone and clustered deployments alike

Objects declared outside the handler stay initialized when the environment is reused

sources.title: Cloudflare: What are Durable Objects?
supports: Each Durable Object has a globally unique name and is single-threaded
Each has its own durable, transactional, strongly consistent storage, accessible only within that object
In-memory state is reset when the object hibernates after being idle

sources.title: Cloudflare Workers: Rate Limiting binding

Limits are local to the Cloudflare location the Worker runs in
The API is described as permissive, eventually consistent, and not intended as an accurate accounting system

sources.title: Detect unmanaged configuration changes to stacks and resources with drift detection
supports: CloudFormation drift detection compares live resource properties with the template; not every resource type or property is covered
Only property values explicitly set in the template or through parameters are compared; default values are not
Resources that do not support drift detection get NOT_CHECKED; a stack with no supported resources is IN_SYNC
Detection on a stack does not detect drift in its nested stacks; run it on the nested stack itself
Detection can run on stacks in CREATE_COMPLETE, UPDATE_COMPLETE, UPDATE_ROLLBACK_COMPLETE, and UPDATE_ROLLBACK_FAILED
The caller needs read permission for each resource, plus cloudformation:DetectStackDrift, DetectStackResourceDrift, and BatchDescribeTypeConfigurations
KMSKeyId is never compared; values the service does not return, and Lambda function code, cannot be compared; attachments across stacks may give inaccurate results
DETECTION_FAILED means detection failed for at least one resource; results are available for the others
Stack-level tags are also checked for drift

sources.title: Detect drift on an entire CloudFormation stack
supports: Detection is asynchronous and must be polled to completion
detect-stack-drift returns a detection ID, describe-stack-drift-detection-status reports progress, describe-stack-resource-drifts returns per-resource results
Only one drift detection operation can run on a stack at a time; it may take several minutes
The guide warns to compare the last drift check time with the result timestamps to avoid using stale data

supports: Drift detection column is Yes for AWS::ApiGatewayV2::Api, Route, Stage, AWS::IAM::Role, AWS::IAM::OIDCProvider, AWS::Lambda::Function, Version, Alias, Permission, and AWS::Logs::LogGroup
Drift detection column is No for AWS::ApiGatewayV2::Integration and AWS::CloudFormation::Stack

The table is described as not exhaustive

sources.title: DescribeStackResourceDrifts

sources.title: StackResourceDrift

Each result carries the Timestamp of when that resource was checked

sources.title: AWS CDK bootstrapping
supports: `cdk bootstrap` deploys the CDKToolkit stack with an asset bucket, an ECR repository, and IAM roles
Each environment (account and Region) must be bootstrapped before deploying into it

sources.title: Bootstrap your environment for use with the AWS CDK
supports: Bootstrapping creates five IAM roles: CloudFormationExecutionRole, DeploymentActionRole, FilePublishingRole, ImagePublishingRole, and LookupRole
Physical names follow cdk-<qualifier>-<description>-<account>-<Region>; the default qualifier is hnb659fds
The deploy role is assumed by the CDK CLI; the CloudFormation execution role is what CloudFormation uses to create resources

sources.title: aws-cdk 2.1145.0 (help output, README, and `cdk bootstrap --show-template`)
supports: Bootstrap template version 32: bucket cdk-<qualifier>-assets-<account>-<region> (versioned, retained on stack deletion, noncurrent versions expire after 30 days), ECR repository cdk-<qualifier>-container-assets-<account>-<region>, five roles, and the SSM parameter /cdk-bootstrap/<qualifier>/version
The CloudFormation execution role gets AdministratorAccess unless --cloudformation-execution-policies or trusted accounts are given
The bootstrap roles trust the account's own principals for sts:AssumeRole; the lookup role has ReadOnlyAccess with a deny on kms:Decrypt

sources.title: Amazon ECS task lifecycle
supports: A task passes through PROVISIONING, PENDING, ACTIVATING, RUNNING, DEACTIVATING, STOPPING, DEPROVISIONING, STOPPED
ACTIVATING is where ECS pulls images, creates containers, and registers load balancer target groups

supports: minimumHealthyPercent is the lower limit of running, healthy tasks during a rolling deployment, as a percent of the desired count, rounded up
maximumPercent is the upper limit of running tasks during a rolling deployment, rounded down; at 200 with a desired count of four the scheduler can start four new tasks before stopping four old ones
The circuit breaker is for deployments whose tasks cannot start; CloudWatch alarms are for failing a deployment on application metrics
By default ECS resolves the image tag in a task definition to a digest, so all tasks of a deployment run the same image

sources.title: How the Amazon ECS deployment circuit breaker detects failures
supports: With the rollback option, a failed deployment is rolled back to the most recent deployment in the COMPLETED state
Stage 1 counts tasks that fail to reach RUNNING; stage 2 counts tasks replaced because of failed Elastic Load Balancing, Cloud Map, or container health checks

sources.title: Amazon SQS standard queues
supports: Standard queues ensure at-least-once delivery; more than one copy of a message might be delivered, and messages may occasionally arrive out of order
Ordering is best effort
SQS stores a message redundantly in multiple Availability Zones before acknowledging SendMessage
Standard queues suit applications that can handle messages arriving more than once or out of order

sources.title: Amazon SQS at-least-once delivery
supports: If a server holding a copy of a message is unavailable when the message is received or deleted, that copy is not deleted and may be delivered again
Applications should be idempotent: not adversely affected by processing the same message more than once

sources.title: Amazon SQS visibility timeout
supports: A received message stays in the queue and is hidden from other consumers for the visibility timeout
If the message is not deleted before the timeout expires, it becomes visible again and can be received by the same or another consumer
The default visibility timeout is 30 seconds; the maximum is 12 hours from the first receive
For standard queues there is no absolute guarantee that a message is not delivered more than once during the visibility timeout
Standard queues allow approximately 120,000 in-flight messages

sources.title: Using dead-letter queues in Amazon SQS
supports: maxReceiveCount is the number of times a consumer can receive a message from a source queue before it is moved to the dead-letter queue
The dead-letter queue must be in the same account and Region as the source queue

For standard queues, a message's expiration is based on its original enqueue timestamp, which does not change when it moves to the dead-letter queue, so the dead-letter queue's retention period should be longer than the source queue's
With maxReceiveCount above 3, a message received 3 or more times without being deleted is moved to the back of the queue

sources.title: Learn how to configure a dead-letter queue redrive in Amazon SQS
supports: By default a redrive moves messages from the dead-letter queue back to their source queue
Redriven messages are considered new messages: they get a new messageID and enqueueTime, and the retention period is reset
Messages cannot be filtered or modified while they are redriven
A redrive task can run for at most 36 hours
Starting a redrive needs sqs:StartMessageMoveTask, sqs:ReceiveMessage, sqs:DeleteMessage, and sqs:GetQueueAttributes on the dead-letter queue and sqs:SendMessage on the destination

supports: SourceArn must be a dead-letter queue whose source is another SQS queue

Only one active message movement task is supported per queue

sources.title: Amazon SQS message quotas
supports: A message is retained for 4 days by default; the minimum is 60 seconds and the maximum is 14 days

A batch request holds at most 10 messages

sources.title: Using Lambda with Amazon SQS
supports: Lambda polls the queue and invokes the function synchronously with a batch of messages
When the function processes a batch successfully, Lambda deletes its messages from the queue
By default, an error anywhere in a batch makes all its messages visible again after the visibility timeout
Event source mappings process each event at least once, and duplicate processing can occur; AWS strongly recommends idempotent function code
The function and the queue must be in the same Region

sources.title: Creating and configuring an Amazon SQS event source mapping
supports: Set the queue's visibility timeout to at least six times the function timeout
The function timeout must not exceed the queue's visibility timeout; Lambda validates this when the mapping is created or updated
AWS recommends a maxReceiveCount of at least 5 on the source queue's redrive policy
Batch size is up to 10,000 for a standard queue; above 10 a batch window of at least 1 second is required
A batch is also limited by the 6 MB synchronous invocation payload

sources.title: Configuring scaling behavior for SQS event source mappings
supports: For standard queues Lambda long-polls the queue, starts with five concurrent invocations, and adds up to 300 more per minute up to 1,250
Maximum concurrency limits the concurrent function instances one SQS event source can invoke; it is between 2 and 1,000 and costs nothing
Maximum concurrency and reserved concurrency are independent; reserved concurrency lower than the total maximum concurrency can lead to throttled messages
With maximum concurrency set, Lambda's optimization down to 2 concurrent invokes at low traffic is not available
sources.note: The page gives no number for how often an idle queue is polled.

sources.title: Handling errors for an SQS event source in Lambda
supports: With ReportBatchItemFailures in FunctionResponseTypes, the function returns the failed message IDs as batchItemFailures[].itemIdentifier and only those become visible again
An empty or null batchItemFailures list means the whole batch succeeded
If the function throws, the entire batch is a failure
An invalid response, an empty or null itemIdentifier, or a message ID that is not in the batch makes the whole batch a failure
With ReportBatchItemFailures activated, Lambda does not scale down polling when invocations fail
A throttled invocation is retried until the message's timestamp exceeds the queue's visibility timeout, and then dropped by Lambda

sources.title: Lambda parameters for Amazon SQS event source mappings
supports: BatchSize defaults to 10 and MaximumBatchingWindowInSeconds to 0
ScalingConfig holds the maximum concurrency; FunctionResponseTypes holds ReportBatchItemFailures

sources.title: AWSLambdaSQSQueueExecutionRole
supports: The permissions Lambda needs on the queue are sqs:ReceiveMessage, sqs:DeleteMessage, and sqs:GetQueueAttributes
The managed policy grants them, and the log permissions, on Resource "*"

sources.title: Amazon S3 Event Notifications
supports: S3 event notifications are designed to be delivered at least once
They are typically delivered in seconds but can sometimes take a minute or longer
SQS FIFO queues are not supported as a destination

sources.title: Event notification types and destinations
supports: Notifications are not guaranteed to arrive in the order the events occurred, and S3's retries can on rare occasions produce duplicates
S3 sends one event entry per notification message
s3:ObjectCreated:* covers Put, Post, Copy, and CompleteMultipartUpload
s3:ObjectRemoved events are not sent for deletes made by a lifecycle configuration; those are s3:LifecycleExpiration events
s3:TestEvent is published when a notification is enabled
Messages can be up to 64 KB; the destination queue must be in the bucket's Region

sources.title: Event message structure
supports: The object key in an event is URL encoded; a space becomes +
The sequencer is a hexadecimal string; for one key, the greater value is the later event
Sequencers can differ in length: left-pad the shorter with zeros, then compare lexicographically
A sequencer cannot order events on different keys
The test message has no Records array: {"Service":"Amazon S3","Event":"s3:TestEvent",...}
eventName omits the s3: prefix
sources.note: The page says the sequencer is "only used with PUT and DELETE requests" and that create events "(PUT requests)" and delete events contain one. It does not say whether an ObjectCreated:Post or a LifecycleExpiration:Delete event carries a sequencer.

sources.title: Granting permissions to publish event notification messages to a destination
supports: The queue's policy allows the s3.amazonaws.com service principal SQS:SendMessage, with conditions on aws:SourceArn (the bucket) and aws:SourceAccount
A queue encrypted with a customer managed KMS key needs a key policy statement for the S3 service principal
sources.note: The page does not mention queues encrypted with SQS-managed keys (SSE-SQS).

sources.title: Using Amazon SQS, Amazon SNS, and Lambda (enabling notifications)
supports: After the notification configuration changes, it usually takes about five minutes to take effect
When a notification is first enabled, an s3:TestEvent occurs

sources.title: AWS::S3::Bucket NotificationConfiguration
supports: Creating the destination and its permissions in the same template as the bucket can produce a circular dependency, because the bucket cannot be created until it has permission to publish and the permission refers to the bucket
QueueConfigurations take one Event, a Queue ARN, and an optional S3Key filter

sources.title: How to retrieve or copy objects based on metadata with conditional reads
supports: GetObject with If-Match returns the object only if its ETag matches the one provided
An object's ETag represents a specific version of the object

sources.title: GetObject
supports: When If-Match does not match, GetObject returns 412 Precondition Failed

sources.title: Manage event ordering and duplicate events with Amazon S3 Event Notifications (AWS Storage Blog)
supports: Duplicate notifications for one object event have the same key, versionId, operation, and sequencer
The post's design stores the newest sequencer per key in DynamoDB and does not update it for an older one
sources.note: An AWS blog post that the S3 user guide links to. Used for the statement about duplicates sharing a sequencer.

sources.title: What is Amazon EventBridge Scheduler?
supports: One-time and recurring schedules
EventBridge Scheduler provides at-least-once event delivery to targets: at least one delivery succeeds with a response from the target
Templated targets exist for SQS, SNS, Lambda, and EventBridge; a retry limit and a maximum retention time for failed triggers can be set

sources.title: Using templated targets in EventBridge Scheduler
supports: A function ARN as the target means Lambda's Invoke operation
The schedule's execution role needs lambda:InvokeFunction for a Lambda target

sources.title: Setting up Amazon EventBridge Scheduler
supports: The execution role is an IAM role that EventBridge Scheduler assumes to call the target; its trust policy names scheduler.amazonaws.com

sources.title: Confused deputy prevention in EventBridge Scheduler
supports: AWS recommends aws:SourceArn and aws:SourceAccount conditions in the execution role's trust policy
The aws:SourceArn value must be a schedule group ARN, not a schedule or a name prefix

sources.title: RetryPolicy (EventBridge Scheduler API)
supports: MaximumEventAgeInSeconds is 60 to 86,400; MaximumRetryAttempts is 0 to 185
Retries use exponential backoff until either limit is reached
sources.note: The page states no default for either value.

sources.title: Schedule types in EventBridge Scheduler
supports: A rate expression is rate(value unit) with minutes, hours, or days
A rate-based schedule without a StartDate starts invoking its target immediately

sources.title: Invoke a Lambda function on a schedule
supports: EventBridge Scheduler invokes a Lambda function asynchronously

sources.title: Amazon EventBridge pricing
supports: EventBridge Scheduler: 14,000,000 invocations a month are free

sources.title: AWS Price List bulk API: Amazon EventBridge, ap-northeast-1
supports: Scheduled invocations in Tokyo (SKU 29C3758CBCYNXH8B): USD 0 for the first 14 million a month, then USD 1.25 per million

supports: DynamoDB collates and compares strings using the bytes of the underlying UTF-8 encoding
